A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReCogDrive and retain the same underlying research framework. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, references, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated analyses and retained dialogue examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReCogDrive results on NAVSIM, component and hyperparameter ablations, QA-data scaling experiments, extended-metric evaluations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original NAVSIM results and additional Bench2Drive, DriveLM, and DriveBench evaluations, alongside decoder comparisons, guidance ablations, robustness tests, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The VLM-conditioned diffusion planner and three-stage training framework remain. v2 explicitly integrates SwiGLU, RMSNorm, RoPE, and QK normalization into the planner, supported by the incremental architectural comparison in Table 4. These are limited architectural refinements. Much of the hierarchical data pipeline and the RL procedure renamed DiffGRPO already appears in v1.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from NAVSIM to CARLA Bench2Drive, adding interactive driving and safety-critical scenarios. DriveLM, previously included as training data, becomes an evaluation benchmark, and DriveBench adds quantitative driving VQA coverage under clean, corrupted-image, and text-only inputs. The existing NAVSIM and driving-QA training coverage largely persists.

E2.justification: New comparisons include TCP variants, ThinkTwice, DriveAdapter, and DriveTransformer on Bench2Drive; GPT-4o, LLaVA, InternVL2, and other VQA models; and alternative trajectory decoders. Within the corresponding NAVSIM Table 1, v2 removes Hydra-MDP-V8192, LTF, BevDrive, and ARTEMIS. ARTEMIS remains in the extended-metric comparison, so it is not removed from the paper entirely.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Bench2Drive route and multi-ability evaluation, GPT-Score VQA assessment, and latency and formatting-error measurements. It adds an InternVL3-2B configuration and changes the reported DiT hidden size/head size from 1536/32 to 384/8. NAVSIM splits and the 3/200/10-epoch training schedule remain. Noise-clipping prose changes from ±3 to ±5, although v2 Table 12 still specifies ±3.

E4.justification: v2 adds decoder and architectural ablations, high-level-command versus chain-of-thought guidance tests, visual-input robustness tests, comparisons of TransFuser and IL/RL trajectories, and categorized failure cases. It removes v1's QA-data scale/quality study and the discount-factor 0.5 condition. The BC-weight and sampling-noise sensitivity studies are retained with revised outcomes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Diffusion-noise standard deviations and group-normalized advantages describe the algorithm rather than uncertainty in reported experimental results.

E6.justification: The main NAVSIM PDMS changes from 89.6 to 90.8, with revised component and sensitivity results; the best reported BC weight changes from 0.01 to 0.001. These accompany changed model settings and do not establish an isolated same-setting gain. New results include Bench2Drive Driving Score 71.36 and success rate 45.45%, DriveBench average 56.71, and decoder timing results. The extended NAVSIM results, including EPDMS 83.6, are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 11 corrects the full diffusion-chain log density by including log p(x_T), omitted from v1 Equation 13, and identifies this prior as independent of model parameters. This is a limited mathematical correction that leaves the policy-gradient objective effectively unchanged. No substantial new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the claimed contribution from NAVSIM planning performance to state-of-the-art NAVSIM and Bench2Drive performance and quantitative driving-VQA capability. v2 also elevates the hierarchical cognitive-data pipeline and named DiffGRPO scheme as central innovations and emphasizes efficient trajectory generation. The underlying VLM-plus-diffusion proposition remains.

C2.justification: New discussion explains optional textual guidance, attributes its limited benefit to NAVSIM diversity, questions whether VQA scores demonstrate visual understanding, and motivates BC regularization over direct KL constraints. Failure analysis adds aggressive progress-seeking, perception weaknesses, unsafe following, and possible metric false negatives. The small-BC-weight interpretation changes from training collapse to greater progress. Conversely, v1's explicit limitation about non-interactive RL training is removed.

D1.justification: Most detailed training schedules, preprocessing, diffusion-step counts, and hardware information persist. v2 adds explicit code and model/data collection links, SGLang annotation tooling, and one-update/no-PPO-clipping implementation notes, while revising model specifications. Reproducibility remains imperfect: its ±5 noise-clipping prose conflicts with ±3 in Table 12, which also retains BC weight 0.01 despite Table 8 favoring 0.001.

R1.justification: The related-work positioning is substantively revised through discussions of GoalFlow, Gen-Drive, R2SE, and Drive-R1, while earlier material such as HybridVLA and DAPO is removed. v2 introduces stronger priority claims for RL applied to driving VLAs and explicitly distinguishes NAVSIM simulator rewards from prior trajectory-distance rewards. These changes extend beyond the switch to author-year citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, several sensitivity analyses move into the appendix, and data construction is reorganized around hierarchical stages. The appendices gain a nine-question discussion and separate failure-analysis and LLM-usage sections, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the overview and planner diagrams and replaces the appendix data-pipeline graphic with a hierarchical diagram in the main text. It adds benchmark, decoder, and guidance tables plus extensive trajectory comparisons and failure visualizations. Existing sensitivity tables are relocated, while the three dialogue figures are retained and renumbered. The document also adopts a different header and typography layout.

improvement.justification: v1's broad planning and cognition claims relied mainly on non-reactive NAVSIM evaluation and illustrative dialogue. v2 substantially strengthens validation through interactive Bench2Drive testing, quantitative VQA evaluation, decoder and guidance ablations, and explicit failure analysis. These address important evidential gaps. The removed data-scaling study, weakened disclosure of non-interactive RL limitations, and new reporting inconsistencies temper the improvement: notably, the ablation prose disagrees with Table 3, and noise-clipping prose conflicts with Table 12. Nevertheless, the broader direct testing and more informative failure evidence provide a substantial net quality gain.
